title: Steinmüller Africa Bursary
description:
Steinmüller Africa is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded to students residing within the Nkangala District Municipality (Mpumalanga) , for studies within the following fields:

Electrical Engineering (BEng Tech) Mechanical Engineering (BEng Tech)

www.zabursaries.co.za is committed to keeping you up to date with the latest bursary opportunities, and this article covers all details about the Steinmüller Africa Bursary.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

Steinmüller Africa recognises the important role that skilled engineers play in building South Africa’s future. The bursary programme is designed to support promising students during their studies by providing:

Financial assistance to help cover the costs associated with completing their qualification. Industry exposure and association with an established engineering organisation, providing students with the opportunity to connect with the professional engineering environment.

Steinmüller Africa is a South African engineering and manufacturing company that provides specialised services and solutions to the energy and industrial sectors. The company has extensive experience in areas such as boiler maintenance, plant construction, fabrication, welding, inspection and engineering services, supporting major industrial facilities across Southern Africa.

With a strong focus on technical expertise, quality and safety, Steinmüller Africa also contributes to the development of skilled professionals within the engineering sector. Through its bursary opportunities, the company aims to support talented South African students pursuing qualifications that can contribute to the country’s engineering and energy industries.

— END —

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

description:
Sasol is inviting students to apply for the Mining Women in Local Communities Bursary Programme , for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded to female students residing in communities around the Sasol Mining Secunda Complex (in Mpumalanga) , for undergraduate studies within the following fields (BEng / BSc):

Electrical Engineering Electronic Engineering Geology Mechanical Engineering Mine Surveying Mining Engineering

The fully funded bursary support students pursuing careers in engineering, mining and related fields. The programme forms part of Sasol Mining’s efforts to expand access to education, develop critical skills and increase opportunities for women in sectors where they remain underrepresented.

Sasol Limited was founded in Sasolburg, South Africa in the year 1950 and is the very first oil-from-coal company. Today, Sasol is a global chemicals and energy company, that is listed on both the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) in South Africa and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in the United States. Sasol is made up of two distinct market-focused businesses: Chemicals and Energy.

The Chemicals Business, made up of Base Chemicals and Performance Chemicals, is aimed at meeting evolving consumer needs, including the demands of a growing and urbanising middle class.

The Energy Business, made up of Mining; Gas and Liquid Fuels, is positioned to be responsive to global trends by providing new energy and mobility solutions, pursuing greenhouse gas emission reductions by developing and growing gas and renewables in Southern Africa and increase cash generation.

Botshelo Safety is a South African health and safety solutions company based in Rustenburg, North West. Established in 2020, the company is a B-BBEE Level 1, majority black-woman-owned business focused on helping organisations create safer and more productive working environments.

The company specialises in the supply of personal protective equipment (PPE) and the management of onsite PPE stores. Its product range includes safety equipment such as head, eye, hearing, respiratory, hand and foot protection, as well as industrial workwear, harnesses and specialised protective clothing. Botshelo Safety serves clients across industries including mining, manufacturing, construction, engineering, food and beverages, agriculture and more.

Beyond supplying safety products, Botshelo Safety provides technology-driven inventory and PPE management services designed to improve stock availability, control costs and ensure employees have access to the appropriate protective equipment. The company has also developed its own Vendor Managed Inventory system to support real-time tracking, reporting and efficient PPE issuing.

As the company continues to expand its operations and support skills development within South Africa, opportunities such as the Botshelo Safety Bursary can provide valuable financial assistance to students pursuing their studies.

The Disability Empowerment Concerns (DEC) Trust is a South African organisation dedicated to advancing the social and economic inclusion of persons with disabilities. title: Australian Government International Scholarship
description:
Australia Awards Scholarships cover the full length of your approved study programme at an Australian university. This includes any required foundation or preparatory courses you need before starting your main qualification.

The scholarship will provide cover for the following expenses:

Full tuition fees paid directly to the university Return flights to Australia, including one economy-class ticket to Australia at the start of your studies and one return ticket at the end Establishment allowance, a once-off payment to help with initial costs such as accommodation, textbooks, and study materials Living allowance (CLE), paid every two weeks to help cover basic day-to-day expenses like food and transport Introductory Academic Program (IAP), a compulsory orientation that prepares you for studying and living in Australia Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the duration of your scholarship, covering essential medical care (excluding pre-existing conditions) English language training (if required), provided either in your home country or in Australia before your course begins Additional academic support, where needed, to help you succeed in your studies Fieldwork support (for eligible Master’s and research students), including return economy-class travel for compulsory research fieldwork either in Australia or in your home country

Scholars will be required to sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia declaring that they will comply with the conditions of the scholarship.
eligibility: You must be a citizen of one of the African, Asian or Pacific countries listed above
You must be 25 years or older on on 1 February 2027

You must be employed at the time of applying for the scholarship

You must meet the minimum English language proficiency of at least 6.5 in IELTS with no band less than 6.0 (an internet based TOEFL score of at least 84, with a minimum of 21 in all subtests, or PTE Academic overall score of 58 with no communicative skill score less than 50). title: West Wits Mining Bursary
description:
West Wits Mining is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for studies within the following fields:

Electrical Engineering Finance Geology Mechanical Engineering Mining Engineering

Students will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience, learn from industry professionals and contribute to shaping the future of Mining in South Africa.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Finance Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

West Wits Mining is a growing South African mining company committed to developing gold and uranium projects within the historic Witwatersrand Basin. Operating near Johannesburg, the company is working to revive some of the region’s most well-known reef systems, including the Kimberley, Main and Bird Reefs, using a phased and sustainable mining approach. With underground operations already underway at its Qala Shallows project and progress toward its first gold production, West Wits Mining is playing an active role in creating new opportunities within the mining sector.

Through its bursary programme, the company aims to support ambitious students who want to build careers in mining, engineering and related fields, while contributing to the future growth of South Africa’s mining industry.

— END —

This bursary listing was last updated in May 2026.

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

title: Absa Historical Debt Relief Programme
description:
The Absa CSI Trust Graduate Historical Debt Relief Programme was created to address the growing challenge of graduates burdened by unpaid historical student debt, that prevents them from receiving their qualifications and entering the job market.

Through this initiative, the Absa CSI Trust provides funding to clear outstanding student debt for graduates from selected higher education institutions who have successfully completed their studies but are unable to obtain their certificates due to unpaid fees. By removing this financial barrier, Absa helps graduates unlock new opportunities to participate fully in South Africa’s economy.

In addition to debt relief, the Absa CSI Trust also supports these graduates in their transition to employment by partnering with the Youth Employment Service (YES). This collaboration connects graduates to real work opportunities, helping them gain experience and establish sustainable careers.

To ensure the smooth rollout of the programme, the Feenix Trust has been appointed to manage and facilitate the debt clearance process on behalf of the Absa CSI Trust.

Khobab Wind Farm is one of South Africa’s large-scale renewable energy facilities, situated near Loeriesfontein in the Northern Cape. The wind farm became fully operational in 2017 and has an installed generation capacity of 140 MW, produced by 61 wind turbines. As part of the country’s Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme (REIPPPP), the facility supplies clean electricity to the national grid and helps diversify South Africa’s energy mix.

The project generates enough renewable electricity to supply the annual needs of approximately 170,000 South African households, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions by displacing electricity generated from fossil fuels. In addition to supporting the country’s transition towards cleaner energy, Khobab Wind Farm contributes to improved energy security through long-term, sustainable power generation.

Beyond producing renewable electricity, Khobab Wind Farm is committed to creating lasting social and economic benefits for neighbouring communities. Through dedicated socio-economic development and enterprise development initiatives, the project invests in education, skills development, healthcare, local infrastructure and community-based programmes designed to improve opportunities and livelihoods within the surrounding areas.

— END —

description:
JG Afrika is inviting students to apply for their Bursary Programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for studies towards a Civil Engineering (BSc or BEng degree).

JG Afrika is a South African engineering and environmental consultancy providing specialised professional services across the infrastructure, built environment and environmental sectors. The firm delivers a broad range of solutions, including civil and structural engineering, environmental consulting, water and infrastructure services, and project management, serving clients in South Africa and other African markets.

With more than a century of experience, JG Afrika combines extensive technical knowledge with a strong understanding of the African operating environment. Its multidisciplinary team works on projects designed to support sustainable development, strengthen infrastructure and create lasting value for clients and communities.

The company is headquartered in Johannesburg and has an established presence in South Africa, as well as operations in countries including Botswana, Mozambique and Lesotho. Its team of approximately 300 professionals includes engineers, environmental specialists, technical experts and support staff who work collaboratively to deliver practical, innovative and environmentally responsible solutions.

Through its combination of engineering expertise, environmental knowledge and African experience, JG Afrika continues to contribute to infrastructure and development projects that balance technical requirements with social, economic and environmental considerations.

title: PRDW Bursary
description:
PRDW is inviting students to apply for their Bursary Programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for studies towards a BSc or BEng studies, within the following fields:

Civil Engineering Mechanical Engineering Mechatronics Engineering

www.zabursaries.co.za is committed to keeping you up to date with the latest bursary opportunities, and this article covers all details about the PRDW Bursary.

View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

PRDW was founded in 1993 in Cape Town, South Africa, and has since developed into an international consulting engineering company serving clients across several regions. Over the years, the firm has expanded its international footprint and now operates through offices in South Africa, Chile, Australia, the United States, Panama and Brazil.

The company provides a broad range of consulting engineering services for marine and coastal developments. Its work can cover the full project lifecycle, beginning with investigations, technical assessments and feasibility studies, and progressing through concept and detailed design, tender documentation and construction supervision. PRDW also supports clients after construction through monitoring, performance assessment and project evaluation.

PRDW’s multidisciplinary team combines expertise across civil, coastal, hydraulic, structural and geotechnical engineering, with specialist knowledge of marine infrastructure and structures. The company also draws on mechanical engineering expertise in materials handling, as well as specialists in oceanography, wave behaviour and coastal processes.

Its wider technical capabilities include physical and mathematical modelling, port and navigation planning, and quantity surveying and contract management. This combination of engineering, scientific and commercial expertise enables PRDW to provide integrated solutions for complex marine, coastal and port-related projects from initial planning through to completion and ongoing evaluation.

— END —

description:
The Chiropractic Association of South Africa is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

CASA is dedicated to shaping the future of chiropractic care in South Africa. To support this mission, they proudly offer yearly bursaries to outstanding South African chiropractic students who demonstrate passion and commitment to their education and career goals.

The Chiropractic Association of South Africa (CASA) represents and promotes the chiropractic profession in South Africa. Its work includes protecting the interests of chiropractors, strengthening the profession’s standing and building relationships with key stakeholders in the healthcare sector.

CASA also aims to encourage interest in chiropractic as a career, particularly among students and young people. Through career guidance and educational initiatives, the association supports individuals who are exploring their study and career options in chiropractic.

As a regulated professional association, CASA works to advance the chiropractic profession while promoting awareness of chiropractic care and supporting the interests of practitioners and future professionals.

description:
The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), in collaboration with the SASOL Foundation, are inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for undergraduate studies , in the following fields, which have been deemed a priority by the CSIR:

Chemical Engineering Computer Engineering Computer Science Data Science Electronic Engineering Genetics / Cell Biology Industrial Engineering Information Technology Material Flow Analysis Mechatronic Engineering Process Engineering / Life cycle assessment System Engineering

The CSIR bursary is merit based and is aimed at full-time, unemployed students who are pursuing qualifications in areas that are deemed a priority by the CSIR (research, technology development and innovation as well as corporate/support areas). The bursary aims to attract suitably qualified applicants, and encourages females, black students and those living with disabilities to apply.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Science Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) is one of South Africa’s leading scientific research and technology development organisations. Established in 1945, the CSIR is a public entity operating under the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI). Its role is to conduct multidisciplinary research, develop innovative technologies, and provide scientific solutions that support South Africa’s economic growth, industrial competitiveness, and social development.

Headquartered on its main campus in Pretoria, the CSIR employs thousands of researchers, engineers, technicians and support specialists who work across a wide range of scientific and engineering disciplines. The organisation collaborates with government departments, universities, industry partners and international institutions to address national and global challenges through research and innovation.

The CSIR’s work is focused on several strategic research areas, including advanced manufacturing and industry, digital technologies, health innovation, energy, the built environment, natural resources and the environment, and defence and security. Through these focus areas, the organisation develops practical technologies and research-driven solutions that improve public services, strengthen industries, and contribute to sustainable development across South Africa and beyond.

— END —

Astronomy Astrophysics Computer Science Mathematics Physics

The South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO) is a national research facility of the National Research Foundation (NRF) that oversees South Africa’s radio astronomy infrastructure and programmes. Shell is a global energy company operating across a broad range of energy and related businesses. Its activities include Integrated Gas, Upstream, Marketing, Chemicals and Products, Renewables and Energy Solutions, and Trading and Supply. The company explores for and produces oil and natural gas, supplies fuels and lubricants, manufactures chemicals and petroleum products, and is also developing lower-carbon energy solutions such as renewable power, hydrogen, biofuels and carbon capture.

In South Africa, Shell has a long-established presence in the energy sector. Its downstream activities include retail and commercial fuels, lubricants, aviation and marine fuels, as well as a nationwide network of Shell-branded mobility and convenience sites. Shell Downstream South Africa currently operates around 580 company- and dealer-owned Mobility & Convenience sites, alongside its lubricants and commercial fuels businesses.

Shell provides fuels, lubricants and related products to customers across a variety of industries, including transport, manufacturing, mining, agriculture, construction, aviation and marine. Its lubricants business supplies products for vehicles, machinery and industrial applications, while its commercial fuels activities serve businesses and other large-scale customers.

Shell’s South African business is also undergoing a significant ownership transition. In July 2026, Shell South Africa Holdings announced an agreement to sell its equity interest in Shell Downstream South Africa (SDSA) to ADNOC Distribution. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to be completed in 2027. Shell has stated that the Shell brand will continue to be present in South Africa through brand-licensing arrangements, while customers will continue to have access to Shell fuels and lubricants.

title: Enel Green Power Bursary
description:
Enel Green Power is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded to students residing within areas around the company’s operations, in the Eastern Cape, Free State, Limpopo, Northern Cape and Western Cape (listed below).

The bursary will cover studies in ANY field (including Technical and Vocational Education and Training programmes, National Diplomas and Degree programmes).

Enel Green Power operations include: Gibson Bay Wind Farm (Eastern Cape) Nojoli Wind Farm (Eastern Cape) Nxuba Wind Farm (Eastern Cape) Oyster Bay Wind Farm (Eastern Cape) Pulida Energy (Free State) Tom Burke Solar (Limpopo) Adams Solar (Northern Cape) Garob Wind Farm (Northern Cape) Karusa Wind Farm (Northern Cape) Soetwater Wind Farm (Northern Cape) Sublunary Trading (Northern Cape) Paleisheuwel (Electra Capital) (Western Cape)

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Bursaries and Scholarships for ANY field here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

Enel Green Power South Africa (EGP SA) was established in December 2008, within the Enel Group. The idea of creating Enel Green Power was to enhance and manage power that is generated from renewable sources around the world.

To date, the company manages more than 1200 power plants across five continents, remaining present with assets that are in operation and those under construction across 20 counties. The company also manages and develops activities within five additional countries, and has more than 60 GW of installed renewable capacity from a number of resources such as solar, wind, geothermal, and hydroelectric.

To date, Enel Green Power plays a vital role in energy transition and remains one of the world’s leading renewable energy companies. Its overall goal is to aid the planet in transitioning into a new era of sustainable and decarbonized energy.

The Ikusasa Student Financial Aid Programme (ISFAP) was established to expand access to higher education for academically deserving South African students from low- and middle-income households. The programme provides comprehensive financial support to help eligible students complete their undergraduate studies at participating public universities, reducing the financial barriers that often prevent students from obtaining a tertiary qualification.

As a registered Public Benefit Organisation (PBO), ISFAP secures funding from a wide range of partners, including government departments, development finance institutions, corporate organisations, charitable foundations, non-profit organisations, and local as well as international donors. description:
The Foschini Group (TFG Limited) is inviting students to apply for their Data Science and Leadership Fellowship, for the 2027 academic year.

The bursary/ fellowship programme is aimed at youth wanting to enhance their skills in one of the most scarce and critical career fields . The award will cover research or coursework Masters Degrees in Data Science or related qualifications.

TFG believes that data science is the key to making educated decisions that will improve the world. They also believe that data scientists are the solution to solving many of the country’s challenges, utilizing insights from big data to help allocate scarce resources where they are needed most.

Through this, TFG hopes to establish a strong pipeline of data specialists for both the business and the nation.

The Foschini Group (TFG Limited), is a South African JSE listed retail clothing group, operating over a number of well-known retail brands. TFG retails a wide variety of items such as footwear, clothing, sportswear, jewellery, and home, furniture appliances, mobile, and tech appliances. Owing to the diversity of its brand, TFG is able to be innovative, pushing the boundaries of both in-store and online retail. Through this, TFG hopes to create remarkable omnichannel experiences for all its clients.

TFG also focuses on establishing a strong network of young data scientists. It believes that data is the key to modern business and the way to maintain being a leading omni-channel retailer. Through this, TFG hopes to mine data from the best and relevant insights, using it to assimilate and interpret a variety of data points in the ever-changing environment.

description:

Motus is a leading multinational automotive group that provides mobility solutions, vehicle products and a wide range of automotive services. Headquartered in South Africa, the company has an extensive presence across the local market while also operating in selected international regions, including the United Kingdom, Australia, Asia, and parts of Southern and East Africa. As one of South Africa’s largest automotive businesses, Motus serves customers throughout the vehicle ownership journey, from vehicle sales and servicing to finance and aftermarket support.

The Group operates through four integrated business divisions: Import and Distribution, Retail and Rental, Mobility Solutions, and Aftermarket Parts. Together, these business units enable Motus to provide manufacturers, fleet operators, businesses and private motorists with a comprehensive range of automotive products and services while maintaining a strong presence across the automotive value chain.

Motus Mobility Solutions specialises in developing and delivering innovative value-added mobility products and financial services that enhance the vehicle ownership experience. Its offerings include vehicle-related financial products, insurance and non-insurance solutions, fleet management services, telemetry, vehicle finance partnerships and consumer mobility solutions. The division works closely with vehicle manufacturers, dealerships, banks, insurers and corporate clients to provide tailored mobility solutions for both individual motorists and commercial fleets.

title: Spirit Education Foundation High School Scholarship
description:
The Spirit Education Foundation Trust, partnered with the Cape Academy of Mathematics, Science and Technology, is inviting students to apply for their scholarship programme for the 2028 academic year.

The high school scholarship programme is open to female students, who will be entering Grade 8 in 2028 .

The scholarship will cover studies at the Cape Academy of Mathematics, Science and Technology (located in Constantia, Cape Town). ( Find out more about the Cape Academy here ).

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other High School Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The Spirit Foundation is a long-standing philanthropic organisation established by the Kilbride family, with more than three decades of work supporting education, community development and wildlife conservation. Its education initiatives focus on creating meaningful opportunities for young people from communities where access to quality education can be limited.

A key part of this work is the Spirit Foundation High School Scholarship Programme, which supports talented young women from financially disadvantaged backgrounds. From 2028, the programme will work exclusively with the Cape Academy of Mathematics, Science and Technology, providing scholarships for female learners who demonstrate strong academic potential and an interest in STEM-related subjects and careers.

Beyond covering educational support, the programme takes a broader approach to scholar development. Recipients have access to mentorship, skills development and holistic support designed to help them succeed throughout their high school years. The programme also aims to develop qualities such as confidence, leadership, creativity and social responsibility, helping scholars prepare for both further studies and future careers.

Through its continued investment in education, the Spirit Foundation aims to give high-potential young women the opportunity to reach their full potential while contributing positively to their communities.

— END —

title: Advance Africa Scholarship
description:
Benefits of the Advance Africa Scholarship:

Remote learning: This allows you to learn at your own pace and in your own time frame. An exceptional curriculum, designed by experts: The Advance Africa scholarship has been developed in partnership with some of the world’s leading tech companies, with classes taught by industry professionals. An opportunity for full-time employment: The scholarship award could also open doors for employment. There are a number of opportunities for the candidate to gain hands-on experience from the bank and engage in project work within teams.

Courses covered by the Advance Africa scholarship:

App Development Business Analytics Cloud Computing Data Analysis Data Science Digital Marketing Project Management Web Development

How the programme works:

During the programme, the successful candidates will be given the opportunity to compete and discover their abilities in various avenues. They will engage in taster sessions, designed to test problem solving, community challenge, conflict resolution, and employability skills. Candidates who successfully complete the course, will be given a badge (Nanodegree) which they can display on various social media platforms, such as LinkedIn. Level 1: The top candidates from the previous level will then be granted the opportunity to engage in intermediate nanodegrees. Level 2: Successful candidates of level one will then be given a scholarship award and enter level two where they will obtain an advanced nanodegree. The duration of this part of the programme is two months. Candidates who successfully completed all assessments and programs, may have the opportunity to be selected for permanent roles.

title: SANParks Bursary
description:
South African National Parks (SANParks) is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded to students residing near National Parks , and will cover undergraduate National Diploma or Degree studies, including but not limited to, the following fields:

Emerging Scarce Skills (including GIS, Analytics, Cyber security, Renewable Energy, Climate Change Adaptation, Biodiversity Economists, Entrepreneurship). Environmental Sciences (including Nature Conservation, Environmental Management, Environmental Science, Green Energy, Environmental Engineering, Sustainable Development and Game Ranch Management). Infrastructure and Built Environment (including Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, Quantity Surveying, Architecture, Project Management). Social Sciences ( including Community Development, Economic Development, Socio-Economic Development and related Development studies). Technical and Artisan Trades (including Electricians, Plumbers, Welders, Millwrights, Mechanics, Technicians, Solar Technicians, Refrigerator Technicians, Water and Wastewater Technicians). Tourism (including Hospitality Management, Tourism Management, Resort Management, Tour Guide, Events and Conference Management).

This external bursary programme hopes to benefit young individuals living in communities near/ surrounding the National Parks.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Environmental Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Tourism and Hospitality Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

South African National Parks (SANParks) is the public entity responsible for conserving, protecting and managing South Africa’s national parks. Established under the National Environmental Management: Protected Areas Act, 2003 (Act No. 57 of 2003), SANParks safeguards the country’s biodiversity, cultural heritage and natural ecosystems while promoting sustainable tourism, environmental education and scientific research.

SANParks currently manages 21 national parks across South Africa, including:

Addo Elephant National Park (near Gqeberha, Eastern Cape) Agulhas National Park (L’Agulhas, Western Cape) Augrabies Falls National Park (near Upington, Northern Cape) Bontebok National Park (Swellendam, Western Cape) Camdeboo National Park (Graaff-Reinet, Eastern Cape) Garden Route National Park (Wilderness, Knysna and Storms River, Western and Eastern Cape) Golden Gate Highlands National Park (Clarens, Free State) Karoo National Park (Beaufort West, Western Cape) Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park (Northern Cape) Kruger National Park (Limpopo and Mpumalanga) Mapungubwe National Park (near Musina, Limpopo) Marakele National Park (Thabazimbi, Limpopo) Mokala National Park (near Kimberley, Northern Cape) Mountain Zebra National Park (near Cradock, Eastern Cape) Namaqua National Park (near Springbok, Northern Cape) Table Mountain National Park (Cape Town, Western Cape) Tankwa Karoo National Park (Northern and Western Cape) West Coast National Park (Langebaan, Western Cape) |Ai-|Ais/Richtersveld Transfrontier Park (Northern Cape)

Beyond conserving wildlife and protecting natural habitats, SANParks works closely with neighbouring communities to promote environmental stewardship, create employment opportunities, support local economic development and encourage responsible tourism. Through community partnerships, education programmes and conservation initiatives, SANParks aims to ensure that South Africa’s protected areas provide lasting environmental, social and economic benefits for both present and future generations.

As part of its commitment to developing future conservation professionals, SANParks also invests in education and skills development through the SANParks Bursary Programme. The programme provides financial assistance to eligible South African students pursuing qualifications in fields that support biodiversity conservation, environmental management and other disciplines aligned with the organisation’s long-term strategic objectives.

— END —

This bursary listing was last updated in July 2026.

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

The South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO) is a national facility of the National Research Foundation (NRF), responsible for managing South Africa’s radio astronomy facilities and strategic investments in the field. description:

Afrimat is a leading South African supplier of construction, industrial and mining materials, serving a diverse range of industries and markets. Its product portfolio includes construction materials such as aggregates, bricks, blocks, ready-mix concrete and paving products, as well as industrial materials including lime and related lime products. The group also supplies bulk commodities such as anthracite, iron ore and manganese.

One of Afrimat’s mining operations is Nkomati Anthracite in Mpumalanga, close to the borders of Eswatini and Mozambique. The operation covers more than 11,000 hectares and includes both the Mangweni underground mining section and the Madadeni opencast operation. Its strategic location provides access to established transport routes connected to the Maputo area, helping to improve logistics efficiency and reduce transportation costs for customers.

Afrimat Nkomati Anthracite produces high-quality anthracite, a form of coal valued for its low sulphur content. Coal extracted from the various mining areas is transported to a central processing facility, where it undergoes beneficiation using a dual-circuit dense-medium separation plant. This process separates and upgrades the coal, producing anthracite suitable for a range of industrial applications.

— END —

title: SADC Essay Competition
description:
Below are a list of questions provided by the SADC to aid you in responding to the aforementioned essay question. When compiling your essay, ensure that you address the questions/ topics listed below in your essay:

1. In your own words, what is industrialisation, and how does it relate to economic development? (this question is worth 10 points) 2. The SADC region is highly committed to implementing activities and programmes, specifically those that promote industrialisation as it is essential to the region’s long-term socio-economic success. Provide 5 specific examples, explain their significance, and elaborate on how they contributed to the development of the region (this question is worth 20 points) 3. What do you think are the focus areas in which you think the SADC region should intervene to maximize the execution of industrialisation-based projects, and what are the barriers that are preventing industrialisation and access to many markets within the area? (this question is worth 20 points) 4. The SADC Industrialisation Strategy (from years 2015 to 2063) and Roadmap hopes to encourage economic and technological transformation within the Region that emphasizes initiatives that build regional value chains. Elaborate on some of the priority areas for regional value chains development in the SADC region and relevant examples (this question is worth 25 points) 5. The SADC hopes to create sustainable economic growth that is beneficial and can withstand challenges. In what ways have other sectors contributed to the increase in industrialisation? Be sure to provide specific examples (this question is worth 25 points)

Successful candidates will receive an equivalent of the prize money in South African Rands, with the top three essays being forwarded to the SADC Secretariat for consideration in its regional competition.
eligibility: You must reside within South Africa
You must currently be in secondary school (high school)
You must be willing and able to travel
application_steps: Your essay should be between 900 and 1000 words
Your essay must be written in English
Your essay must be in your own words and not written with assistance from anyone else
Your essay must be in electronic version, submitted in Microsoft Word document format
Your essay must be written in Arial font, with a 1.5 line spacing
Your essay must state your full name as it appears on your Identity Document/ Passport
Your essay must address the topic and promote the SADC’s Objectives and Common Agenda

title: Wells Mountain Initiative Scholarship
description:
The scholarship will provide partial cover for the following expenses: tuition and fees, books and course materials/ supplies, accommodation, meals and transportation. It is NOT a full scholarship, therefore students will be responsible for covering any additional fees.

WMI award between 80 and 100 scholarships each year, to the average value of $1500 USD (and sometimes up to $3000 USD).

Selection process and dates:

Applications will be reviewed via an in-depth multi-step review process, between April and July 2026 Scholarship recipients will be announced on 1 August 2026 (on the WMI website and on their Facebook page) and unsuccessful applicants will receive a regret email First installment of scholarships will be wired during September 2026

www.zabursaries.co.za is committed to keeping you up to date with the latest bursary opportunities, and this article covers all details about the WMI Bursary.
eligibility: You must be from a country in the developing world (this includes South Africa – see full list of developing countries here)
You must be NOT be older than 35 years on 1 August 2026
You must have completed Matric (secondary school) OR be currently in Matric with excellent academic results
You must be applying to university OR currently studying towards your first undergraduate degree or diploma
You must be studying in your home country or another country in the developing world
You must plan to live and work in your own country once you have graduated
You must have participated in volunteer service before applying for this scholarship and be committed to volunteering within your community during your studies
You must have some study funding available but are not able to go to attend university without financial assistance
You must be committed to maintaining above-average results in all university studies
You must be committed to becoming an ambassador for community service and engagement
You must be able to perform, record, and document 100 hours of community service activities throughout the year
You must complete the Academic Semester Report & Community Service Report for WMI Scholars twice a year
You must NOT plan to study in the United States, Canada, Australia, UK or Western Europe
You must NOT be a family member of WMI staff or of WMI Scholars
You must download and read the WMI Scholarship Information Flyer before applying
application_steps: National ID document/ alternative ID Document
Grades transcripts from the school you attended
National exam results (if applicable)
Headshot photograph
University tuition fees structure (you can provide it directly from the website if you have not been accepted yet)
2 recommendation letters (read the WMI recommendation letter guidelines here)
Personal statement (350 to 500 words)

Essay (maximum 1000 words), on the topic “If you were awarded $1000 to support a service project to help your community, what issue would you address? Why is this a current or continuing issue within your community? Why is this issue important to you? Who would benefit and what would be the impact? How would you measure the success of the activity? Please provide a detailed budget in USD for all expenses.” (Note: this is a hypothetical situation and should not be considered a request for funding)

description:
The Energy Mobility Education Trust is inviting students to apply for their scholarship programme, for the 2027 academic year.

Scholarships will be awarded for undergraduate and postgraduate studies , within these fields, at selected institutions ( WITS, UJ, UP, NWU, UL, UWC ):

Accounting Actuarial Science Computer Science Engineering Information Science Mathematical Science Science Statistical Science Technology

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Computer & IT Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Science Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The Energy Mobility Education Trust was established in 2014 by bp Southern Africa (bpSA), originally operating as the BPSA Education Foundation Trust. As its mission expanded beyond its initial focus, the organisation adopted the name Energy Mobility Education Trust to better reflect its broader commitment to supporting education and skills development in South Africa.

The Trust is dedicated to empowering talented young Black South Africans by improving access to tertiary education, accredited training programmes and career-focused skills development opportunities. Through financial assistance and educational support, it aims to help students gain the qualifications needed to build successful careers and contribute to the country’s future workforce.

Over the past decade, the Trust has invested approximately R262 million in education, providing funding to more than 4,387 students as they pursue higher education and professional development.

— END —

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

description:
The UK Government is inviting students to apply for the Chevening Scholarship, for the 2027-2028 academic year .

The scholarship will cover 1-year Master’s Degree studies in ANY subject, at any university within the United Kingdom , start in September/ October 2027. Applicants can use the Chevening course finder to find a suitable qualification.

The award is aimed at students who demonstrate outstanding academic ability. The programme aims to allow students the opportunity to focus on achieving both their academic and professional goals whilst having the opportunity to study abroad. Chevening hopes to foster passionate individuals who have a clear vision of how to change the world.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other International Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The Chevening Scholarship is the UK Government’s flagship international scholarship programme, designed to support talented and ambitious individuals from around the world. Established in 1983, the programme provides exceptional professionals with the opportunity to pursue postgraduate study in the United Kingdom while developing their leadership skills, professional networks and global perspectives.

Funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), together with partner organisations, Chevening supports scholars who have the potential to make a meaningful contribution to their communities, countries and professions. Through access to world-class education and a global network of like-minded professionals, the programme aims to help develop future leaders who can drive positive change both locally and internationally.

The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) is South Africa’s central bank, whose main purpose is to maintain price stability for sustainable economic growth within the country. SARB was established in the year 1921 after the passing of the “Currency and Bank Act of 10 August 1920” in Parliament. Before the Bank was established, South African commercial banks issued banknotes to the public.

The SARB are responsible for the following: ensuring that the banking, money and financial system in South Africa achieves the community requirements and keeps up to date with international developments, as well as helping the government (and other economic community members) of South Africa with data for macroeconomic policy, and lastly to provide the South African community and international stakeholders with feedback regarding the countries monetary policy and economic standing.

The Chemicals division manufactures a broad portfolio of products used in industries such as agriculture, automotive, construction, healthcare, consumer goods and manufacturing. description:

Each year, scholarships are awarded to 60 students who are entering Grade 8 in 2028 (currently in Grade 6 in 2026) , who demonstrate strong academics and are in financial need.

Bergvliet High School Camps Bay High School Claremont High School Groote Schuur High School Herschel Girls High School Pinelands High School Rondebosch Boys High School Rustenberg Girls High School SACS (South African College) High School Springfield Convent Senior School St. George’s Grammar School Westerford High School Wynberg Boys High School Wynberg Girls High School

Students For A Better Future (SBF) is a scholarship programme established and funded by the Andreas and Susan Struengmann Foundation, a philanthropic organisation founded in 2007. The Foundation focuses on improving access to quality education in South Africa, with a particular emphasis on supporting talented learners from disadvantaged communities in the Western Cape.

In addition to the SBF scholarship programme, the Foundation has supported several educational initiatives, including the Sue Struengmann Initiative at the University of Cape Town (UCT) and the development of educational opportunities for learners in communities such as Imizamo Yethu in Hout Bay.

The Andreas and Susan Struengmann Foundation aims to empower young people through education by nurturing confident, responsible and well-rounded individuals. Its long-term vision is to help develop future leaders who can make meaningful contributions to South Africa while becoming active and engaged global citizens.

— END —

title: Fine Music Radio (FMR) Bursary
description:
The FMR Bursary Trust Awards will include the following rounds:

The first round (application) will be through a pre-recorded audition video, and thereafter a final round will be held in the Baxter Concert Hall, in Rondebosch. The competition is made up of 4 categories: Classical Voice, Classical Instrumental, Jazz Vocal/ Instrumental and African Music. The Preliminary round performance is made up of pre-recorded unlisted YouTube videos, which must be presented for adjudication. The link must be included in your application. Up to 3 applicants will be chosen from each category for the final round. (Please email bursaryawards@fmr.co.za if you have trouble uploading your video to YouTube). The final rounds will be held in the Baxter Concert Hall (on 28 July at 6:30pm for Classical and 31 July at 6:30pm for Jazz/ African). It will also be broadcast by Fine Music Radio and the competitors will each receive a copy of the broadcast for their own non-commercial use. Final round competitors must provide FMR with full details including names and instruments of ensemble/ accompanist by no later than 15 July 2026. By applying for this bursary competition, applicants agree that the FMR Bursary Trust may record and use any of the performances in the competition at their discretion. The Adjudication stage will include the adjudication panel making a decision on the selected candidates. Their decisions are final and no appeal will be considered. Feedback on the decisions will only be revealed after the final round of the competition. The preliminary and final rounds will be assessed individually, therefore the performance scoring is not combined. Applicants will be adjudicated based on general presentation and balanced programme compilation. Applicants in the Jazz and African categories may also receive marks towards the instrumentation and arrangement of the pieces, as well as leadership within the ensemble. Repertoire: applicants must produce a programme of up to 15 minutes duration, which must include at least two pieces of contrasting style. The Classical Vocal category must contain at least one opera aria and one art-song. The African Music category must show skill on at least two instruments, one of which can be voice. Competitors should repeat the works from the preliminary round in the final, but changes in repertoire may be allowed if submitted before 15 July 2026. Backline ensemble should not exceed four persons.

description:
The Garden Route District Municipality (GRDM) is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Government Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The Garden Route District Municipality (GRDM) is a Category C municipality in the Western Cape, South Africa. It was previously known as the Eden District Municipality, with the name officially changed to Garden Route District Municipality in 2018.

The district is bordered by the Sarah Baartman, Overberg, Cape Winelands and Central Karoo district municipalities. It consists of seven local municipalities: Bitou, George, Hessequa, Kannaland, Knysna, Mossel Bay and Oudtshoorn.

Known for its diverse landscapes, the Garden Route stretches from coastal towns and forests to inland farming areas. The region is also a major tourism destination, attracting visitors with its beaches, nature reserves, wildlife, scenic routes and outdoor adventure activities.

— END —

This bursary listing was last updated in September 2026.

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

title: MINDS Scholarship
description:
The Mandela Institute for Development Studies (MINDS) is inviting African students to apply for the MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development .

The scholarship is available for Postgraduate (Honours or Master’s degree) studies within Africa , in any field, at approved institutions. The scholarship is available to students from any African country, to study outside of their own country .

The MINDS Scholarship Programme aims to create leaders who have a continental development mindset; leaders who will encourage greater cohesion and cooperation between African countries.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other International Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The Mandela Institute for Development Studies (MINDS) is a continental institute that seeks to address the short, medium, and long-term development challenges in Africa in a holistic and comprehensive manner.

The following programmes are offered by MINDS: African Heritage Programme, Economic and Regional Integration Programme, Youth Programme on Elections and Governance, Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development, Programme de bourses d’études pour le développement du leadership and African Youth Networks Movement.

The MINDS Scholarship Programme for Leadership Development in Africa was initially launched in 2017, with the goal of developing young leaders with a continent-wide development mindset and leaders who can facilitate greater cooperation between African countries. The Scholarship Programme aims to allow for students to become immersed in the richness and diversity of an African country and its communities has to offer, by offering students the opportunity to study in an African country other than their country of residence.

— END —

The Northern Cape Provincial Government is responsible for governing South Africa’s largest province by land area and delivering a wide range of public services to its residents. Working within the framework of the Constitution, the provincial government develops legislation, implements national and provincial policies, and oversees key sectors such as education, healthcare, social development, agriculture, transport, economic development and environmental management.

In partnership with the national government, district and local municipalities, and other public institutions, the Northern Cape Provincial Government strives to improve service delivery, stimulate economic growth and enhance the quality of life of communities across the province. Through strategic planning, infrastructure investment and community development programmes, it supports sustainable development while addressing the unique needs of both urban and remote rural areas.

— END —

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

description:
The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung (KAS) is inviting postgraduate students to apply for the KAS-SAIIA Scholarship Programme , for the 2027 academic year .

KAS-SAIIA Scholarships are available for studies in either Johannesburg or Cape Town.

Johannesburg Scholarship Programme For Master’s degree studies in one of the following fields: International Relations/ Development Studies/ Political Science/ Economics/ Law/ Journalism (or a related humanities or social sciences discipline). For studies at University of the Witwatersrand (Wits). Based at SAIIA’s Johannesburg office. The office focuses on: Economic resilience, African diplomacy, Governance.

Cape Town Scholarship Programme For Master’s degree studies in Political Science . For studies at: University of Cape Town (UCT)/ Stellenbosch University (SU)/ University of the Western Cape (UWC). Based at SAIIA’s Cape Town office. The office focuses on: Climate change, Futures and foresight research.

Applicants may only apply for one programme. Applications for both Johannesburg and Cape Town will not be considered.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to choose the programme that best aligns with their academic and career interests.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Masters degree Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other University-specific Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung (KAS) is a German political foundation dedicated to strengthening democracy, the rule of law, good governance and international cooperation. Named after Germany’s first post-war Chancellor, Konrad Adenauer, the foundation promotes political dialogue, civic education, policy research and leadership development in countries around the world. In South Africa, KAS operates from offices in Cape Town and Johannesburg, where it collaborates with universities, research institutions, government bodies and civil society organisations on projects that support democratic governance and sustainable development.

The South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA) is an independent, non-profit public policy think tank that conducts research and analysis on South African, African and global affairs. Through evidence-based research, policy dialogue and public engagement, SAIIA contributes to informed decision-making on issues such as foreign policy, governance, economic development, climate change and international relations. Headquartered at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, the institute also has a presence in Cape Town and works with partners across Africa and beyond.

— END —

title: Canon Collins RMTF Scholarship
description:
Canon Collins Trust, partnered with the Ros Moger and Terry Furlong (RMTF) group, are inviting students to apply for scholarship funding, for the 2027 academic year .

Scholarships will be awarded to students from South Africa, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Swaziland, Zambia , for Postgraduate studies (Masters or PhD) in South Africa , within the following fields:

Justice (including Climate Justice, Law, Economics and Politics) Education policy and practice Humanities (including Literature, History, Anthropology and the Arts)

The scholarship aims to support exceptional individuals who are committed to social justice in southern Africa and for whom a postgraduate qualification is an essential tool in working to create an open and just society.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other International Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The Canon Collins Trust has been investing in higher education across southern Africa since 1981, helping talented students access opportunities that enable them to become leaders and create positive change in their communities. Since its establishment, the Trust has supported more than 4,000 scholars from 14 southern African countries, building an extensive network of graduates working in fields such as education, law, public policy, science and social justice.

Today, the Trust primarily provides postgraduate scholarship programmes in partnership with universities and funding organisations in South Africa, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Malawi, while selected partner initiatives also support undergraduate studies. In addition to financial assistance, Canon Collins scholars benefit from leadership development, networking opportunities and an active alumni community committed to advancing social and economic development throughout the region.

One of the Trust’s long-standing partnerships honours the legacy of Ros Moger and Terry Furlong, two respected London educators who believed strongly in the transformative power of education. Since 2001, friends, family and supporters have raised funds in their memory to provide scholarships for deserving southern African students. The Ros Moger and Terry Furlong (RMTF) Scholarships have helped more than 120 students pursue postgraduate studies in areas including education, health, the humanities and the arts.

— END —

description:
Scholarships will cover up to 50% of the course fees per year (for the full three-year degree).

The competition is based on Visual Storytelling – a skill that all four schools at The Open Window emphasise. To enter the competition, candidates are required to demonstrate their visual storytelling skills by responding to the theme: “What’s in a story?”

Open Window wants applicants to create a series of 4 images or frames inspired by the theme. Applicants are free to use any format, any approach, or any visual medium – as long as you can submit a story of your own in response to ‘What’s in a story?’ For example, think of stop motion, comics, photographs, typography, sound, animation, 3D objects, digital designs/ illustrations, textiles, ceramics, film, etc.

The Canon Collins Trust has been investing in higher education opportunities for talented students from southern Africa since 1981. ** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Bursaries and Scholarships for females here . View our other International Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG) is a non-profit, public charity that has been established since 1981. MMEG supports and empowers women from developing countries by providing them with education grants, aiding them in establishing their personal future and the future of their country.

The organization draws its inspiration from Margaret McNamara, who had a goal of promoting education and gender equality. Margaret was the wife of the World Bank’s 5th President and used her influence to be an advocate for these elements of development programs. Before her death, Margaret received the highest civilian distinction in the United States, the Medal of Honour, in recognition of her important contributions.

description:
The South African National Society (SANS) is inviting students to apply for the Killie Campbell Bursary, for the 2026 (September) and 2027 academic year.

Bursaries will be awarded to students pursuing Postgraduate studies, in a History related topic (the area of research, or dissertation must be on a topic relating to South Africa, preferably KwaZulu-Natal history).

SANS has been awarding bursaries for the past 40 years, to financially assist postgraduate history students.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other History Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The South African National Society (SANS) goals are stipulated in the constitution. They aim to create love and appreciation for South Africa’s historical, natural, and cultural heritage as well as its citizens. The SANS aims to further promote appreciation for all the aspects that are integral to the citizens of the county, and provide general support and publicity to the South African Heritage Resources Agency and the Amafa/ Heritage KwaZulu-Natal in their aim of preserving the cultural resources of the country. SANS also helps in supporting other organizations/ bodies facing a similar task.

Dr Killie Campbell was an avid collector, historian and supportive member of the Society. After she passed away in 1965, her collection was bequeathed to the University of KwaZulu-Natal and is now the Killie Campbell Africana Library. The Killie Campbell Bursary was formed in her honour.

description:
Canon Collins Trust is inviting students to apply for the University of London LLM Scholarship, for the 2027 academic year .

Scholarships will be awarded to students from South Africa, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe , for distance learning studies towards a Postgraduate Certificate, Postgraduate Diploma and/or the Master of Laws (LLM) at the University of London .

This scholarship supports mid-career professionals committed to social justice who wish to pursue further legal studies to strengthen their impact and drive positive change.

Applicants can enter the programme at different levels and are not required to complete the full qualification. Those with an LLB may enter directly at LLM level, while other applicants can progress from a Postgraduate Certificate towards the LLM.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other International Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Law Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The University of London is a federation of higher education institutions with a long-standing commitment to making university study accessible to students in the UK and around the world. Established by Royal Charter in 1836, the University has played an important role in expanding access to higher education.

Today, the University of London provides a variety of study opportunities, including flexible and distance-learning programmes that allow students to pursue qualifications from different locations. Its international approach to education makes it a suitable study destination for students seeking high-quality UK qualifications while studying outside the UK.

The Canon Collins Trust was founded in 1981 in memory of Canon John Collins, a prominent British campaigner who was involved in social justice, anti-apartheid and human rights movements. The organisation supports education and social change, with a particular focus on Southern Africa.

Through its scholarship programmes and wider work, the Trust supports talented students, researchers and activists who have the potential to contribute to positive change in their communities. Its education initiatives are designed not only to assist students financially, but also to build a network of individuals committed to human rights, social justice and development in Southern Africa.

Volkswagen Group Africa has been part of South Africa’s automotive industry for decades, with its roots in the country dating back to 1946. The company operates its manufacturing facility in Kariega (formerly Uitenhage), Eastern Cape, where it produces Volkswagen vehicles and components for the wider Volkswagen Group.

As one of the Eastern Cape’s major private-sector employers, Volkswagen Group Africa has developed strong connections with communities in and around its manufacturing operations. Its corporate social investment programmes focus on areas such as education, skills development, youth empowerment and community upliftment.

Through its Volkswagen for Good initiative, the company has supported a range of projects aimed at creating lasting social impact. These have included literacy programmes designed to improve reading outcomes among young learners, employee-led volunteering through the Show of Hands programme, and initiatives that encourage young people to develop entrepreneurial skills.

Volkswagen Group Africa has also provided educational support through programmes such as the Children of VW Bursary, which assists eligible children of Volkswagen employees with access to quality schooling and additional support in subjects such as Mathematics and Science.

The company’s community initiatives reflect its broader commitment to helping young South Africans access education, develop practical skills and build stronger opportunities for their future.

title: Dube TradePort Bursary
description:
Dube TradePort is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded to students residing in KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) , for undergraduate studies within the following fields: Agricultural Studies (Crops/ Plants) Built Environment Engineering Information Technology

Students must be enrolled at one of these institutions : Durban University of Technology (DUT) Mangosuthu University of Technology (MUT) University of KwaZulu-Natal (UKZN) University of Zululand (UniZulu)

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Agriculture & Maritime Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other IT Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

Dube TradePort Corporation was established in 2003 as a public entity owned by the KwaZulu-Natal Provincial Government. The organisation is responsible for the development and management of the Dube TradePort, a strategically located economic and logistics hub near King Shaka International Airport in KwaZulu-Natal.

At the centre of the development is the Dube TradePort Special Economic Zone (SEZ), which was created to attract local and international investment, encourage trade and support the growth of key industries. The precinct brings together facilities for manufacturing, logistics, warehousing, agriculture, aviation-related activities and commercial development, providing businesses with access to modern infrastructure and transport connections.

Dube TradePort also plays an important role in promoting economic development in KwaZulu-Natal by supporting businesses, attracting investment and creating opportunities for employment and skills development. Its location provides direct access to air, road, rail and sea freight networks, helping businesses connect with markets across South Africa, the African continent and international destinations.

Through the continued development of the Special Economic Zone and its associated infrastructure, Dube TradePort Corporation aims to strengthen KwaZulu-Natal’s position as a competitive business, trade and logistics destination while contributing to long-term economic growth in the province.

— END —

description:

Bursaries will be awarded undergraduate for studies in a field of study related to ICT (Information and Communications Technology) .

In 2020, ISPA launched the ISPA Inspires Educational Sponsorship Programme after concluding its long-running teacher training initiative, which helped more than 3,000 teachers gain ICT skills over 19 years.

ISPA Inspires focuses on supporting talented young South Africans who want to pursue careers in the ICT and Internet industries. Through educational sponsorships, the programme helps students access relevant tertiary education and develop the skills needed for South Africa’s growing technology sector.

title: South African National Seed Organization (SANSOR) Bursary
description:
SANSOR is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for Postgraduate degree studies (Honours, Masters or PhD) within the seed industry .

The bursary aims to financially assist deserving postgraduate students, who wish to conduct high quality scientific research in these areas:

Agronomy Biotechnology Entomology Genetics Horticulture Molecular Plant Biology Pasture Science Plant Breeding Plant Pathology Plant Physiology

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Science Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

Bursaries are awarded based on academic merit, and bursaries are only awarded for a period of 1 year at a time. Bursary recipients may receive funding for further years of study based on satisfactory academic performance.

Bursary awards are paid directly into the student’s account at their university, in two tranches.

Apart from financial support, bursary recipients will also be able to attend workshops to gain employment skills, field trips to seed companies to learn more about the seed industry, and networking opportunities with seed industry professionals.

The South African seed industry has a long history, with its first organised industry association established in 1940 through the South African Seedmen’s Association. Since then, the sector has undergone significant development, evolving from a largely production-focused industry into a highly competitive and innovative market serving South Africa’s diverse agricultural needs.

In 1989, the South African National Seed Organization (SANSOR) was established as the representative body for the local seed sector. Its role is to promote and protect the interests of the seed industry while supporting collaboration, responsible industry practices and the continued development of South Africa’s seed trade.

— END —

The Paper Manufacturers Association of South Africa (PAMSA) is inviting students to apply for their Bursary and Research Programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Stellenbosch University University of Witwatersrand University of the North-West University of Pretoria

For over 10 years, the PAMSA Bursary and Research Programme has been empowering South African chemical engineering students, by way of funding, academic support, and practical research opportunities. The programme focuses on developing future industry leaders by encouraging research that addresses real challenges within the pulp and paper sector.

Through this initiative, students gain valuable experience in areas linked to sustainability, renewable resources, recycling, and improving manufacturing efficiency. The bursary programme also contributes to the growth of South Africa’s circular bioeconomy by supporting innovative research projects that promote the responsible use of natural and recycled materials within the industry.

The Paper Manufacturers Association of South Africa (PAMSA), founded in 1992, are known for promoting paper as a renewable and recyclable material for packaging, communication and various other applications.

PAMSA represent more than 90% of South Africa’s paper, packaging and tissue manufacturers, in fact they are called the ‘voice of the pulp and paper industry’.

The Canon Collins Trust has a long history of supporting students from Southern Africa, with its scholarship programmes dating back to 1981. Over the years, the Trust has helped thousands of scholars from across the region access higher education and develop their skills.

description:
The Trust will select 4 to 5 students to receive the bursary, which will provide funding to the value of R40 000 each, towards the last year of your LLB studies.

Scholars will be selected based on 5 main criteria: 1) Academic record – candidates must have a strong academic record for their years of study completed or show improvement. 2) References – candidates must provide references who can attest to their studies. 3) Working experience – candidates with paid or voluntary work experience in the field of study will receive preference. 4) Leadership qualities – candidates will be required to prove how their leadership skills have developed in the workplace, in their studies or personal life. 5) Commitment to your community and country – candidates who show a strong interest in positively contributing to the prosperity of their community or to southern Africa, will receive preference. 6) Application – candidates who demonstrate a good command of the English language, answer all of the questions properly and completely and complete the application and deliver all supporting documents in a timely manner, will receive preference.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an interview in November 2025, and thereafter all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Magalies Water is a South African state-owned regional water utility that provides bulk water and sanitation services to municipalities, mines and industrial customers across parts of Gauteng, Limpopo and North West.

Established in 1969, the organisation was originally created to supply water to platinum mining operations in the Rustenburg and Thabazimbi areas. Today, Magalies Water supplies treated bulk water to municipalities and other large customers, playing an important role in supporting communities and economic activity.

The utility sources raw water from river systems linked to dams managed by the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS). It then treats the water at its treatment plants to ensure it is suitable for consumption. Its main water resources are located within the Crocodile River and Pienaars River catchment areas.

Its work focuses on expanding access to housing finance for low- and middle-income households, while supporting initiatives that contribute to better housing opportunities and broader socio-economic development.

Through its role in the housing finance sector, the NHFC works to address some of the financial and structural barriers that prevent South Africans from accessing affordable housing.

South32 is a global mining and metals company that was established in 2015 following the demerger of assets from BHP Billiton. The company produces and develops commodities that are important to modern infrastructure and the transition towards a lower-carbon economy. Its portfolio includes aluminium, alumina, manganese, nickel, silver, lead, zinc, copper and metallurgical coal, with operations and development projects spanning Australia, Southern Africa and the Americas.

In South Africa, South32 has a long-standing presence, including manganese operations in the Northern Cape and a regional office in Johannesburg. The company’s activities contribute to the supply of materials used in industries such as construction, manufacturing, technology, transportation and energy.

South32 also places emphasis on developing future skills and supporting communities where it operates. Its education initiatives include financial assistance for students through its South African bursary programme, helping talented young people pursue tertiary studies and build careers in fields relevant to the mining and metals industry.

The Dr Xolani Mkhwanazi South32 Bursary Scheme was named in honour of the late Dr Xolani Mkhwanazi, who served as a South32 Non-Executive Director from 2015 until his death in 2020. A respected scientist and business leader, Dr Mkhwanazi had extensive experience in South Africa’s mining, metals and technology sectors. South32 renamed its South African bursary scheme in his honour in FY2021, reflecting his commitment to developing young talent and building the industry’s future skills base.
