Cape Town is the largest city in the Western Cape and the oldest continuously established city in South Africa. Often referred to as the Mother City, it is internationally recognised for its spectacular natural scenery, including the famous Table Mountain, one of the New7Wonders of Nature. The city is also known for its rich cultural heritage, thriving tourism industry and role as South Africa’s legislative capital.

The City of Cape Town is a metropolitan municipality responsible for delivering a wide range of essential local government services to residents and businesses. These include water and sanitation, electricity distribution, waste collection, road and stormwater maintenance, traffic management, public transport, environmental management, spatial planning, building development approvals, municipal law enforcement, fire and rescue services, libraries, parks, recreation facilities and other community services.

The municipality covers the entire Cape Peninsula and surrounding metropolitan area, incorporating diverse communities from the city centre to the northern and southern suburbs, the West Coast, Helderberg, Cape Flats and the far South Peninsula. For planning and service delivery purposes, the City is divided into eight planning districts, enabling it to coordinate infrastructure, development and municipal services across one of South Africa’s fastest-growing metropolitan areas.

title: SEDISA Trust Bursary
description:
The SEDISA Trust is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded to Black female students , for Undergraduate (Diploma, Degree), Honours, and Masters studies in ANY field .

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Bursaries and Scholarships for female students here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

SEDISA is a Black woman-owned education trust and a shareholder of KAEFER Thermal Contracting Services (Pty) Ltd, which was established in 2010. The Trust was founded to support the educational advancement of young Black South African women by providing bursaries for tertiary studies.

Its bursary programme focuses on academically capable students who have the potential to succeed but may not have the financial resources needed to pursue higher education. Through this support, SEDISA aims to remove financial barriers and give young women the opportunity to build brighter futures through education.

Beyond financial assistance, the Trust seeks to encourage determination, ambition and a commitment to personal growth. Its mission is to inspire students to make the most of their educational opportunities, pursue their goals with confidence and remain resilient in the face of challenges.

Since launching its bursary initiatives in 2012, SEDISA has supported more than 30 students with tertiary education funding. The organisation has also set its sights on expanding its impact, with a long-term goal of providing at least 40 bursaries each year to deserving students.

— END —

title: Kader Asmal Fellowship Programme
description:
The Embassy of Ireland in South Africa, is inviting students to apply for the Kader Asmal Fellowship Programme, for the 2027/ 2028 academic year . The fully-funded scholarship programme is managed by the Irish Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

The Kader Asmal Fellowship Programme is for South African students to pursue Master’s level studies, in Ireland’s top-rated Higher Education Institutions .

12 annual scholarships will be awarded for Postgraduate Study in the following areas:

Business, Economics, Project Management, Strategic Management, Leadership and related Climate Change & Resilience, Environment, Marine, Sustainable Development, GIS Development Studies, Human Rights, Peace Studies, International Relations, Politics, Public Policy Education Engineering and Sustainable Technology Food Science, Food Engineering and Food Industry Health, Medicine, Pharmacy, Biotechnology and related Information Systems, Communications Technology, Digital Media International Law, Human Rights Law, Business Law Sociology, Social Policy, Social Research and related Tourism and Hospitality Women’s Studies, Gender Studies and Equality Studies

See which courses are covered here: Directory of Programmes/ eligible courses (.pdf).

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other International Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The Kader Asmal Fellowship Programme was established by the Government of Ireland in honour of the late Professor Kader Asmal, a distinguished South African lawyer, human rights activist and politician. Professor Asmal lectured in law at Trinity College Dublin for 27 years, specialising in labour, human rights and international law. He also co-founded the Irish Anti-Apartheid Movement and was a member of the ANC negotiating team that helped secure South Africa’s transition to democracy.

The Kader Asmal Fellowship Programme, which forms part of the Ireland Fellows Programme, aims to develop future South African leaders by providing fully funded Master’s degree opportunities at leading higher education institutions in Ireland. The programme seeks to strengthen skills and leadership capacity, support the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and foster lasting partnerships between Ireland and South Africa through academic, professional and cultural exchange.

— END —

This bursary listing was last updated in July 2026.

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

description:

Final-year undergraduates may apply for the PGDip or Honours in one of the listed degrees.

The SAPOA Bursary Trust was formed in 2009 and is primarily funded by SAPOA members. The aim of the bursary is to: promote transformation, redress the past, promote the property sector to youths and address the current and future skills shortage.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Construction & Building Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Property-related Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The South African Property Owners Association (SAPOA) was established in 1966 to represent and promote the interests of South Africa’s commercial and industrial property sector. As a member-led organisation, SAPOA works to support private property ownership, investment and sustainable development across the industry.

SAPOA strives to be recognised as a leading property association, both within South Africa and internationally, by contributing to the growth, professionalism and advancement of the property sector.

Through the SAPOA Bursary Fund, the organisation aims to help address the shortage of skilled professionals within South Africa’s commercial property industry. The bursary programme provides financial support to academically deserving students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds, with a particular focus on developing young Black South Africans.

By investing in students pursuing property-related studies, SAPOA hopes to expand access to education, develop future industry professionals and contribute to the transformation and long-term growth of South Africa’s commercial property sector.

description:
The Institute of Municipal Engineering of Southern Africa (IMESA) is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

Established in 1961, the Institute of Municipal Engineering of Southern Africa (IMESA) is a professional organisation that supports municipal engineering and infrastructure development across Southern Africa. The Institute provides a platform for engineers, municipalities, academics and industry partners to exchange knowledge, promote best practices and contribute to the sustainable delivery of public infrastructure. IMESA has grown to represent more than a thousand individual members, together with numerous affiliate organisations operating within the engineering and built environment sectors.

IMESA’s mission is to advance excellence in municipal engineering by encouraging professional development, technical innovation and collaboration. Through training, conferences, publications and industry partnerships, the Institute helps strengthen engineering capacity while supporting municipalities in delivering reliable infrastructure and essential public services.

Introduced in 2000, the IMESA Bursary Scheme assists academically deserving students pursuing qualifications in civil and infrastructure engineering at accredited South African tertiary institutions. The programme aims to reduce financial barriers for promising students while also recognising the achievements of IMESA members and their dependants, helping to develop the next generation of municipal engineering professionals.

— END —

This bursary listing was last updated in July 2026.

title: SARB Bursary
description:
The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) is inviting students to apply for their external bursary scheme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for undergraduate degree studies , including but not limited to, fields related to functions and activities of the South African Reserve Bank (SARB). (For example: Accounting, Actuarial Science, Economics, Finance, Information Technology, Law, Mathematical Statistics, as well as Dentistry, Medicine and Social Work and other scarce skills fields ) .

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Accounting & Finance Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Computer & IT Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The South African Reserve Bank (SARB) is South Africa’s central bank, whose main purpose is to maintain price stability for sustainable economic growth within the country. SARB was established in the year 1921 after the passing of the “Currency and Bank Act of 10 August 1920” in Parliament. Before the Bank was established, South African commercial banks issued banknotes to the public.

The SARB are responsible for the following: ensuring that the banking, money and financial system in South Africa achieves the community requirements and keeps up to date with international developments, as well as helping the government (and other economic community members) of South Africa with data for macroeconomic policy, and lastly to provide the South African community and international stakeholders with feedback regarding the countries monetary policy and economic standing.

— END —

This bursary listing was last updated in June 2026.

SA Bursaries wishes you the best of luck with your application! Please remember to SHARE this page with anyone you know who may be in need of bursary funding.

You must have achieved a minimum overall average of 70% for your Matric June exams

You must be from a disadvantaged background

title: NFVF Bursary
description:
The National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF) is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for Undergraduate and Postgraduate (National Diploma/ Degree) studies , within Film or Television-related fields (excluding any performing arts, acting, music, dancing, and any other course not within the Film and TV category).

The aim of the NFVF bursary programme is to stimulate and develop skills of candidates, who wish to follow a career within the film & TV industry.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Film & TV Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF) was formed in order to ensure substantial growth of the film and video industry in South Africa, by providing funding for the development and training of filmmakers, as well as for producing, developing, distribution and marketing of films

The NFVF is a statutory body and an agency of the Department of Sports, Arts and Culture (DSAC). The main objectives of the NFVF are to: increase the accessibility of South African films; to increase the amount of films in South Africa and the amount of producers for previously disadvantaged backgrounds; to increase the amount of training within the film industry and in scarce skills areas; to locally and internationally promote the film industry of South Africa.

— END —

title: SAMSTIP Teacher Intern Bursary
description:
The bursary will cover the following expenses: UNISA tuition fees, prescribed textbooks, small monthly stipend and an allowance for transport and accommodation. Bursary recipients will also receive the following benefits: training at ISASA member schools, provided with teaching and learning resources and technology, mentorship from qualified school teachers, academic enrichment programme.

After graduation, students will be required to teach at a public school – the period of employment will be equal to the duration of bursary funding received.

Shortlisted candidates will be contacted and may be invited to complete an entrance assessment. After the entrance assessment, candidates will be invited for an internal interview, thereafter candidates will be interviewed by a potential host school and provisionally placed. Shortlisted candidates will also be required to apply to UNISA (applications open between August and September each year) and thereafter a final selection will be made. Successful applicants will be formally notified in writing and instructed to report for duty at their Professional Development Host School.

Samancor Chrome is a South African mining and ferrochrome producer with a history dating back to 1975. The company was formed through the merger of SA Manganese Ltd and Amcor Ltd. SA Manganese had been established to mine manganese ore in the Northern Cape, while Amcor focused on mineral extraction and the production of ferroalloys for the steel industry.

The company was previously associated with BHP Billiton and Anglo American, which held 60% and 40% respectively. Following the sale of the chrome business to the Kermas Group in 2005, Samancor Chrome Holdings (Pty) Limited was established as the company’s sole shareholder. Samancor Chrome is now a privately owned company.

Samancor Chrome’s business is centred on the mining and beneficiation of chrome ore and its conversion into ferrochrome, an important raw material used in stainless steel production. The company’s chrome mining activities are located along the eastern and western limbs of South Africa’s Bushveld Igneous Complex, one of the world’s major sources of chromite. Its mining operations include Eastern Chrome Mines in the Steelpoort Valley and Western Chrome Mines in the North West Province.

The company currently operates six ferrochrome smelting operations: Ferrometals, Middelburg Ferrochrome, Tubatse Ferrochrome, Tubatse Alloy, TC Smelter and Dikwena Chrome. Together, these facilities provide Samancor Chrome with substantial ferrochrome production capacity. The company states that its combined capacity exceeds 2 million metric tons of charge chrome per year, although actual production varies according to market conditions.

Samancor Chrome supplies ferrochrome and chrome ore to markets in South Africa and internationally. More than 90% of the company’s chrome alloy production is exported to stainless-steel producers around the world, highlighting its role in the global chrome and ferroalloy supply chain.

— END —

Ricci Schwab Lyons Scholarship :

Named in memory of Ricci Schwab Lyons, honors her legacy as a distinguished partner and Chief Operating Officer at Fasken in Johannesburg. Its origins date back to 1912, when it was established as the Department of Irrigation, before evolving through several name changes to become the Department of Water and Sanitation in 2014.

The DWS is responsible for developing and implementing national policies, legislation and strategies relating to water resource management, water supply, sanitation, and water conservation. Its mission is to ensure that all South Africans have equitable access to safe, reliable water and dignified sanitation services while promoting the sustainable use and protection of the country’s water resources to support social and economic development.

Through its Learning Academy and other skills development initiatives, the Department of Water and Sanitation supports the development of qualified professionals in the water sector. The department offers bursaries and training opportunities to students pursuing studies in scarce and critical skills fields related to water and sanitation, helping to build the expertise needed to manage South Africa’s future water resources.

EY, formerly known as Ernst & Young, is one of the world’s leading professional services organisations and a member of the global “Big Four” accounting firms. The company adopted the simplified EY brand in 2013, although its history stretches back more than 175 years through a series of predecessor firms. The modern organisation was established in 1989 following the merger of Ernst & Whinney and Arthur Young & Co.

Today, EY operates as a global network with a presence in more than 150 countries and territories, employing over 400,000 professionals who provide services to businesses, governments and non-profit organisations. Its multidisciplinary expertise spans assurance, consulting, strategy and transactions, tax, and a growing range of technology, sustainability and managed services that help organisations navigate an increasingly digital business environment.

EY serves clients across a wide variety of industries, including financial services, energy, mining, manufacturing, technology, telecommunications, healthcare, life sciences, consumer products, retail, real estate, infrastructure, government, automotive, and the public sector. Through its combination of industry knowledge, innovation and global reach, the firm supports organisations in improving performance, managing risk and creating long-term value.

title: Rhodes Trust Scholarship
description:
The Rhodes Trust is inviting students to apply for the Rhodes Scholarships for Southern Africa, for the 2027 academic year .

Scholarship will be awarded to students from Southern Africa (South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia and eSwatini) , for Postgraduate studies at the University of Oxford, in the UK, commencing in October 2027 .

Candidates should read the Rhodes Trust Scholarship Conditions of Tenure (.pdf) for courses covered.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Postgraduate Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

The following scholarships will be awarded:

4 scholarships for applicants from South Africa 1 scholarship for an applicant from KwaZulu-Natal province 1 scholarship for an applicant from these countries: Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, Malawi and eSwatini 1 scholarship for an applicant from these schools/ past pupils: Bishops Diocesan College (and its partner schools: St Cyprian’s School, St George’s Grammar School, Herschel Girls School and LEAP 1 School), Paul Roos Gymnasium (and its partner schools: Rhenish Girls’ High School and Bloemhof Girls’ High School), South African College School (and its partner schools: Sans Souci Girls’ High School and Rustenburg High School for Girls), St Andrew’s College (and its partner school: Diocesan School for Girls)

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend a social engagement and a final interview. The interviews will take place by the end of November, in the region you have applied at (except for the Selection Committees for KwaZulu-Natal, BLMNS, regions and schools that will meet in September and October).

Successful candidates will received feedback by email (unsuccessful candidates will not be contacted).

The Rhodes Scholarship is the oldest international scholarship programme, allowing candidates from around the world to study at the University of Oxford, in the United Kingdom. The first Rhodes Scholarship was awarded in 1902.

The fully-funded scholarship is administered by the Rhodes Trust in Oxford, and is awarded to more than 100 candidates every year, for full-time postgraduate studies at one of the world’s leading universities – the University of Oxford.

— END —

The Legal Practitioners’ Fidelity Fund (LPFF), formerly known as the Attorneys Fidelity Fund (AFF), is a statutory fidelity guarantee fund established under the Legal Practice Act 28 of 2014. Its primary purpose is to protect members of the public who suffer financial loss after money or property entrusted to a legal practitioner is stolen or misappropriated while being held in trust during the course of legal practice.

By providing compensation in qualifying cases, the LPFF helps strengthen public confidence in South Africa’s legal profession. The Fund plays an important role in maintaining trust in attorneys and trust account advocates by ensuring that clients have financial protection when trust funds are unlawfully misused. In addition to administering claims, the LPFF supports the legal profession through initiatives such as legal education, bursaries and regulatory funding in accordance with the Legal Practice Act.

description:
Eskom is inviting students to apply for their bursary programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for studies within the following fields:

Eskom offers bursary opportunities to talented South African matriculants and tertiary students who are interested in pursuing careers in engineering and the energy industry. The programme provides financial support to students studying selected engineering and non-technical fields, while helping develop the skills and expertise required to support the future of South Africa’s energy sector.

** RELATED BURSARIES **

View our other Engineering Bursaries and Scholarships here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships OPEN for application here .

Eskom is South Africa’s state-owned electricity utility and one of the country’s largest energy organisations. It was established in 1923 as the Electricity Supply Commission (ESCOM) to develop and coordinate the country’s electricity supply. The organisation later became known as Eskom.

Today, Eskom plays a central role in South Africa’s electricity system. Its operations cover the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity, with a large fleet of power stations supplying electricity to the national grid. Its generation portfolio includes coal-fired power stations as well as the Koeberg Nuclear Power Station in the Western Cape.

Eskom also operates and maintains much of South Africa’s high-voltage transmission network, moving electricity from power stations to distribution networks and large customers. Through its distribution operations, electricity is supplied to municipalities, businesses and households across the country.

The utility has undergone significant restructuring in recent years as part of efforts to improve operational performance, financial sustainability and reliability. Eskom’s former integrated structure has been separated into three operating entities: Eskom Holdings, Eskom Generation and Eskom Transmission, with the distribution function also being reorganised as part of the broader reform of the electricity sector.

Eskom remains a key institution in South Africa’s energy landscape, while the country continues to diversify its electricity supply through renewable energy, private generation and other energy-sector developments.

— END —

The Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) is one of South Africa’s leading scientific research and technology development organisations. Established in 1945, the CSIR is a public entity operating under the Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI). Its role is to conduct multidisciplinary research, develop innovative technologies, and provide scientific solutions that support South Africa’s economic growth, industrial competitiveness, and social development.

Headquartered on its main campus in Pretoria, the CSIR employs thousands of researchers, engineers, technicians and support specialists who work across a wide range of scientific and engineering disciplines. The organisation collaborates with government departments, universities, industry partners and international institutions to address national and global challenges through research and innovation.

The CSIR’s work is focused on several strategic research areas, including advanced manufacturing and industry, digital technologies, health innovation, energy, the built environment, natural resources and the environment, and defence and security. Through these focus areas, the organisation develops practical technologies and research-driven solutions that improve public services, strengthen industries, and contribute to sustainable development across South Africa and beyond.

Valterra Platinum, previously known as Anglo-American Platinum, is one of the world’s top producers of platinum group metals (PGMs). The company operates mines, smelting plants, and refineries in South Africa and Zimbabwe, and sells its metals to customers all over the world.

After separating from its former parent company, Anglo American plc, Valterra Platinum is now an independent business. It is listed on both the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa and the London Stock Exchange in the United Kingdom.

As an independent company, Valterra Platinum can now set its own goals and strategies. It focuses on working efficiently, protecting the environment, and creating long-term value. The company manages the entire process of producing PGMs – from mining them out of the ground to delivering them to the market.

Valterra Platinum aims to be the leading producer of platinum group metals in the world. It is committed to safety, sustainability, and making a positive difference, guided by its purpose: Unearth Value to Better Our World.

Founded in 1918, the South African Society of Music Teachers (SASMT) is the longest-established professional organisation representing music educators in Southern Africa. description:
The Pharmaceutical Society of South Africa invites students to apply for bursary funding, for the 2027 academic year .

The Pharmaceutical Society of South Africa (PSSA) is the country’s oldest professional organisation representing pharmacists and the pharmacy profession. Its origins can be traced back to 1885, when a small group of pharmacists gathered in King William’s Town (now Qonce) to establish a professional network for the industry. Over the following decades, regional pharmaceutical societies were established across South Africa, eventually leading to the creation of the Pharmaceutical Society of South Africa in 1946 through the unification of these organisations.

Today, the PSSA is dedicated to advancing the pharmacy profession by promoting high standards of professional practice, ethical conduct, continuing professional development, and lifelong learning. The Society works closely with pharmacists, pharmacy support personnel, educators, researchers, healthcare organisations, and policymakers to improve pharmaceutical care and encourage the safe and effective use of medicines. Through advocacy, education, professional networking, and member support, the PSSA continues to strengthen the role of pharmacists in delivering quality healthcare and improving patient outcomes throughout South Africa.

— END —

title: SAICA Thuthuka Bursary
description:
The South African Institute of Chartered Accountants (SAICA) is a South African based accountancy body, in fact they are the top accountancy body in the country. The history of the company dates back to 1894, when it was formed in Johannesburg as “The Institute of Accountants and Auditors”. SAICA is one of the global leading Institutes and currently boasts more than 36 000 members. These bursaries aim to provide financial assistance to Western Cape students who are deserving in terms of merit and need.

www.zabursaries.co.za is committed to keeping you up to date with the latest bursary opportunities, and this article covers all details about the ASSET Bursary.

View our other Bursaries and Scholarships for ALL fields of study here . View our other Bursaries and Scholarships for students within the Western Cape here . View our other Bursaries OPEN for application here .

The Association for Educational Transformation (ASSET) is a non-profit organisation based in the Western Cape that has been supporting access to higher education since its establishment in 2003. The organisation grew from the long-running bursary programme created by the South African Institute of Race Relations (SAIRR) in 1972, continuing its legacy of helping academically deserving students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Today, ASSET provides financial assistance to approximately 500 students each year.

ASSET’s bursary programme is designed to reduce financial barriers to tertiary education by supporting students who have the potential to succeed but cannot afford the cost of their studies. The programme is made possible through the generous contributions of individual donors, businesses, trusts, foundations, and international partners, enabling more South African students to achieve their academic and career goals.

— END —

eligibility: You must be a South African citizen

You must be registered one of these institutions within the Western Cape: University of Cape Town, University of the Western Cape, University of Stellenbosch or Cape Peninsula University of Technology (the bursary will NOT fund studies at private institutions)

You must pass the means test and fall within the “Missing Middle” (have a total monthly income of less than R18 000 for a family with 2 children – this can increase by R2000 per child for up to four children, with a combined income of between R350 000 and R600 000 per annum)

Preference will be given to students who have achieved above average results, in subjects related to their course of study
Preference will be given to students who have an excellent attendance record and have been committed to the ASSET Learner Development Programme (Saturday School)

title: Nedbank Bursary
description:
Nedbank is inviting students to apply for their External Bursary Programme, for the 2027 academic year .

Bursaries will be awarded for studies towards a first Undergraduate or Honours degree/ diploma , to address scarce-skills shortages in the country, with a specific focus on (STEM) studies:

Green Economy skills are areas of study focused on improving social well-being and social equity, as well as greatly reducing environmental risks and ecological insufficiency (including reduction of carbon emissions and pollution, enhancing natural capital and increasing energy and materials efficiency).

Nedbank will be awarding bursaries to academically deserving students, in financial need, who are studying or wish to study but are lacking the financial means to do so.

The history of Nedbank dates back to 1831 when the Cape of Good Hope Bank was established. Following numerous name changes; structural changes and rebranding; the Nedbank Group was then formed in 2003.

As one of the four largest banks in South Africa, Nedbank is also one of the newest. The bank is present in 6 countries within the Southern African Development Community (SADC), as well as owning banks and subsidiaries in Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Swaziland, Malawi and Lesotho.

The services offered by the bank include wholesale and retail banking services, wealth management offering, insurance and asset management.

In 1969, Nedbank listed their ordinary shares on the JSE Limited – today they are within the “Top 40” companies on the JSE and boast a market capitalisation of R93 billion.

title: Transnet Bursary
description:
The bursary will provide cover for the following expenses: tuition fees, textbook allowance, accommodation, meals and experiential training. The bursary award will be renewed each year based on satisfactory academic performance.

Students may be required to do vacation work at Transnet during the June/ July or December/ January holidays.

After graduation, bursars may be is required to work at Transnet for the equal duration of the bursary award, depending on the availability of vacancies.

www.zabursaries.co.za is committed to keeping you up to date with the latest bursary opportunities, and this article covers all details about the Transnet Bursary.

Shortlisted candidates will be contacted by February 2026 – if you do not receive any feedback by the end of February, please consider your application unsuccessful.

Shortlisted candidates will be required to attend an interview by the Transnet Academy (in Johannesburg, Bloemfontein, Cape Town and Durban), before final selection is made.

Students will also be required to undergo a medical fitness assessment and must provide satisfactory academic results before selection can take place.
